cases.source_anchor: Section 3 Algorithm 2, page 5; Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, pages 7 and 8
cases.rationale: Both endpoints follow one initialized Delayed SAPO policy and its shared monitoring and switch mechanism.
The delay is unknown at action choice and the source availability set uses a strict inequality.
The source fixes adversarial losses and all delays obliviously, while stochastic arm losses are iid.
The objective is expected regret against the best fixed arm, not a dynamic or pathwise comparator.

cases.rationale: The original wording sounded like two delay statistics, but the source defines sigma_max as the time maximum of one outstanding-feedback count sigma(t).

cases.source_anchor: Theorem 4.1, page 7; Appendix F Algorithm 8, pages 36--37
cases.rationale: Removing log K uses a distinct appendix modification and cannot be transferred to the main algorithm unchanged.
The hard parameter may depend on the universally quantified policy; exchanging that order strengthens the theorem.
The Q and R bounds are explicit theorem assumptions tied to the support geometry.
The faithful contract was sound, but the injected-drift contrast incorrectly summarized the source as globally at-most-s rather than an s-unit support representation that permits zero coefficients.
The original contract called p and q cardinalities, but the source makes them positive real parameters controlling Phi bounds; only k and s describe support/group counts.
The two lower-bound branches use p and q in different stated roles and retain the q^(1/3) factor.
Each application supplies a specific action geometry and embedding; the original locator did not identify the corollaries or pages.
The source specifies a raw-reward softmax-gradient update but does not introduce a separately named reward baseline, so the original baseline phrase was ambiguous.
Every score starts at zero and the policy uses the fixed source learning-rate convention.
Theorem 1 is explicitly two-armed and the general K-arm analysis is separate and incomplete in general.

cases.source_anchor: Reward-family definition, page 1; Theorem 1 and Equation (8), pages 4--5
cases.rationale: Theorem 1 imports bounded support through membership in F, whose definition appears on page 1 rather than in the theorem text alone.
The upper and lower results have different threshold constants, directions, and scopes.

cases.source_anchor: Theorem 2, page 6; Theorem 3 and conjecture discussion, pages 7--8; Theorem 4, page 9
cases.rationale: The positive K-arm result is the identical-gap Theorem 4, while the Delta/K threshold remains conjectural and is motivated by Theorems 2 and 3.
